theme: Unit 15 review, The New Covenant Inaugurated, Matthew
memoryText: You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Peter spoke these words in the region of Caesarea Philippi, a place full of temples to pagan gods. Jesus had asked, “Who do you say that I am?” and Peter answered for the group.

“You are the Christ.” The word means the Anointed One, the Messiah, the king who was promised to David and for whom Israel had waited. Peter is saying that all the Old Testament hopes are fulfilled in Jesus. Everything you read in the Old Testament, the promised seed, the prophet like Moses, the son of David, the servant, and the king, was pointing to him.

“The Son of the living God.” This phrase goes further. “Son of God” was a title for the king, but Peter’s words, heard with the later Gospel, mean more. And he says “the living God,” in contrast to the dead idols all around. Jesus is the Son of the one real, living God.

Jesus answered that this was not revealed by flesh and blood but by the Father in heaven. Faith is a gift. If you confess Jesus as the Christ, the Son of the living God, it is because the Father has opened your eyes.

And on this confession, Jesus said he would build his church. The church is a community of people who say what Peter said. Carry this sentence with you as the center of the whole unit. Every chapter of Matthew is meant to bring you to say it from the heart.
unitRecap: Unit 15 opened the New Testament with Matthew’s Gospel, and it showed that Jesus is the one for whom the whole Old Testament was waiting. His genealogy gathered Abraham and David. He was the new Israel, called out of Egypt, baptized in the Jordan, and tested in the wilderness, where he answered every temptation with Scripture. He was the new Moses, who gave the Sermon on the Mount from a mountain, showing that the law was always aimed at the heart and that he came to fulfill it, not abolish it. He taught us to pray to our Father, to seek first the kingdom, and to build our lives on the rock. His miracles showed the kingdom’s power over disease, nature, demons, sin, and death, and his parables showed that it begins small and grows. Peter confessed that he is the Christ, the Son of the living God, and Jesus began to teach that the Christ must suffer. On the mountain the Father said, “Listen to him.” In Jerusalem he rode in as the humble king, taught the two great commandments, and warned of judgment. At the Last Supper he gave his body and blood for the new covenant. At the cross, he bore the Father’s wrath, the veil was torn, and the way into God’s presence was opened. On the third day he rose and sent his disciples to all nations with all authority and with his presence. Two doctrinal days taught the Trinity and baptism. The King has come, and the kingdom has been inaugurated. The rest of the New Testament shows how it spreads.

reviewQuestions.question: How does Matthew’s genealogy establish Jesus as the fulfillment of the OT covenants?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Think of Matthew 1:1 and the three sets of fourteen. What do Abraham and David represent, and why do the four women matter?

reviewQuestions.question: What does the Sermon on the Mount reveal about the relationship between law and gospel?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Think of the Beatitudes for the poor in spirit, the demand to go beyond the letter of the law in 5:21-48, and the impossible standard in 5:48. How does it drive us to Christ?

reviewQuestions.question: What does it mean that Jesus came not to abolish the law but to fulfill it?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Look at Matthew 5:17-20 and 22:37-40. How does Jesus keep the law, complete it, and bring it to its goal?

reviewQuestions.question: How does Matthew present the death and resurrection of Jesus as the climax of Israel’s story?
reviewQuestions.prompt: Consider the Last Supper and the new covenant, the cry from Psalm 22, the torn veil, the centurion, and the Great Commission.

prayerPrompts: Thank God for Jesus, the Christ, the Son of the living God.
Tell him what you have seen in the King through Matthew.
